messages:
carla: Heads-up — we need a capacity plan for bringing the new 30B-v2 quant variants into Dedicated across us-west, eu-central, and ap-southeast. Goal is to support our PLG baseline and a plausible marketing surge. Asking for recommended concurrency targets per GPU class and suggested autoscale buffer.

ben: Quick Q — what are the latency SLOs we should size to? p50/p95/p99 targets?

carla: Target SLOs: p50 < 70ms, p95 < 200ms, p99 < 420ms for short chat-ish seqs (~64 tokens). For longer contexts (~512) p95 < 900ms. If that affects GPU choices we can trade cost vs latency.

sophia: I ran microbenchmarks across A100-80GB, H100-80GB, and L4s with q4f16 / q8_0 quant configs. Paste of condensed results (tokens/sec, 64-token seq, single-stream concurrency 1):
```
H100, q4f16: 245 toks/s
A100, q4f16: 180 toks/s
L4, q4f16: 95 toks/s
H100, q8_0: 330 toks/s
A100, q8_0: 250 toks/s
L4, q8_0: 120 toks/s
Context 512 drops throughput ~3.2x for H100-q4f16.
```
Also saw kernel differences: cutlass-fused gives slightly better tail latency at short contexts; cuda-kernel-v2 beats for longer contexts due to better KV cache handling.

liam: ran a quick sim with the fleet-mix heuristic. Command I used:
```
./sim --model 30b-v2-q4f16 --region us-west,eu-central,ap-southeast --fleet H100:12,A100:6,L4:4 --qps 2200 --p50 70 --p95 200
```
Output summary: steady-state capacity supports ~1650 qps with concurrency envelope 1.35x. Surge (x2 traffic for 10m) required envelope ~1.8x before autoscale catches up.

infra-bot: sim-report 1841234590: recommended concurrency multipliers: steady: 1.35, short-surge: 1.8, planned-maintenance: 1.6. Estimated GPUs to reserve per region (rounded): us-west H100:12, A100:4; eu-central H100:6, A100:6; ap-southeast mix leaning A100/L4 for cost.

ben: Can we translate that into per-customer concurrency and billing impact? If we reserve 1.35x headroom we pay for more idle capacity.

carla: Rough numbers: assuming 30% qps on H100s, reserved H100 fleet adds ~22% to baseline monthly committed cost vs dynamic. But it cuts p99s by ~40% for peak workloads. I added a short spreadsheet summary here: https://internal.redwood/cap-plan/1841234567 (private).

sophia: Important quality note — q4f16 on some eval suites shows a drop vs full-fp of ~2.4% macro F1 on our safety/regression set for edge prompts. We should canary q8_0 and q4f16 with eval hooks that run per-rollout. Suggest routing 5% traffic to quant variant for 48h with continuous eval.

liam: Agree on canary. Also propose autoscale policy tweak: faster scale-up threshold (10s) for head-of-line latency spikes, slower scale-down (10m) to avoid thrash during marketing bursts.

sre-oncall: Please add routing fallback policy: if p99 > 600ms for 2m, fallback to lighter model (compat-13B) rather than queueing. Avoids user-visible timeouts.

carla: Added to the runbook draft. Next steps: 1) eng-ml to produce per-variant eval delta sheet, 2) eng-platform to run regional sims with the proposed fleet mixes and give final GPU reserve numbers, 3) SRE to sign off on autoscale thresholds and fallback. Can folks ack?

ben: ack :thumbsup:

sophia: ack, will post eval delta table by EOD tomorrow

liam: ack, starting regional sim runs now — will push CSVs to the shared sim bucket

infra-bot: noted — created ticket INFRA-7832 to track reserve requests and canary rollout config

carla: Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after sims finish.

sre-oncall: will validate fallback playbook once canary config is available. :white_check_mark:
